title: C# Questions & Answers - Type Conversion in Expressions
sourceFile: Expressions Type Conversion - C# Multiple Choice Questions - Sanfoundry.html
description: This set of C# MCQs focuses on "Type Conversion in Expressions".

questions.question: What is the primary need for 'Type Conversion' in C#?

options.text: To store a value of one data type into a variable of another data type
To increase the execution speed of the program
To prevent compile-time errors when assigning incompatible types
Both A and C are correct

questions.explanation: Type conversion is necessary when you need to assign a value of one type to another, ensuring type safety and satisfying the compiler's requirements for compatible assignments.

questions.question: What are the two types of 'Data Conversion' available in C#?
questions.explanation: C# supports implicit conversion (automatic for widening types) and explicit conversion (requires a cast for narrowing types).

questions.question: Which of the following follows the correct order of 'Implicit Conversion' based on data type compatibility?
questions.explanation: In C#, a 'char' can be implicitly converted to an 'int', and an 'int' can be implicitly converted to a 'float' without loss of magnitude.

questions.question: For the following C# code, which statement is true about the data type conversion?

options.text: The compiler will generate a runtime error
The conversion from int to long is implicit; no error occurs
Specifying an explicit cast to long is mandatory here

questions.explanation: The result of (num1 + num2) is an 'int'. Since 'int' is smaller than 'long', the compiler performs an implicit conversion to assign the value to the 'total' variable.

questions.question: Which of the following data types can an 'int' be implicitly converted to in C#?
questions.explanation: C# allows implicit widening conversions. An 'int' (32-bit) can be implicitly converted to 'long' (64-bit), 'float', or 'double' because these types have a larger range.

questions.question: In which case is the compiler UNABLE to convert data types implicitly?
questions.explanation: Conversion from 'int' to 'uint' requires an explicit cast. Even though they are both 32-bit, 'int' can contain negative values which cannot be represented in 'uint'.

questions.question: What is a common disadvantage of using Explicit Conversion (casting)?

options.text: It makes the program memory heavier
It can result in loss of data or precision
It makes the code execute slower

questions.explanation: Explicit conversion is used when narrowing types (e.g., double to int). This can result in loss of fractional parts or overflow if the source value exceeds the target type's range.
